NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 6 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 18 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 13, 9:50 PM ET

Brock Bowers is the top-projected tight end on the Week 6 DraftKings main slate at 18.9 DraftKings points for $7,500, against Buffalo. Trey McBride (17.1, $7,200) and Tyler Warren (14.2, $5,300) are next.

Isaiah Likely returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.73 projected points per $1,000 at $4,800.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 13, 9:50 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 6

Brock Bowers, LV vs BUF ($7,500)

Brock Bowers carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 18.9 DraftKings points at $7,500. That is 1.8 points clear of Trey McBride. The model gives him 8.1 targets on 28.2 routes. The salary works out to 2.52 projected points per $1,000, 5th of 18 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 19.0 points with a simulated floor of 7.3 and a ceiling of 38.6, and he holds 15% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 5.5-point underdog at home against Buffalo, with an implied team total of 24 in a game totaled at 53.5.

Trey McBride, ARI at LAR ($7,200)

Trey McBride projects 2nd at the position with 17.1 DraftKings points at $7,200. The model gives him 10.7 targets on 41.2 routes. The salary works out to 2.37 projected points per $1,000, 8th of 18 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 17.1 points with a simulated floor of 6.4 and a ceiling of 35.6, and he holds 5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 12.5-point underdog on the road against the Rams, with an implied team total of 19.5 in a game totaled at 51.5.

Value: Harold Fannin Jr., CLE vs BAL ($4,100)

Harold Fannin Jr. projects for 11.1 DraftKings points at $4,100, which works out to 2.70 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 18 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 7.2 targets on 30.9 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Fannin averaged 11.2 points with a simulated floor of 2.7 and a ceiling of 26.4, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cleveland is a 4.5-point underdog at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 18.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.
